pr_title: Setup Storybook in UI package & Cleanup
pr_body:
## What is the current behavior?

1. Storybook is not setup in `packages/ui`.
2. `Accordion`, `Alert`, and `Avatar` needs TypeScript Cleanup.

## What is the new behavior?
1. Storybook is setup in `packages/ui`.
2. `Accordion`, `Alert`, and `Avatar` is cleaned.

## Steps to test

Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository:

- cd `packages/ui`
- `npm run storybook`
- Confirm `Accordion`, `Alert`, and `Avatar` stories load correctly.

### Demo

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7220167/228275569-f3e57851-18c0-434d-9190-06f71cc01330.mov


### Ref
https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/6249

edit. @MildTomato added some more components 

fixes #12417

@gitstart hey folks. need to careful editing the props on components. even though it's a bit of a mess, and things look unused, it breaks app builds as they are using props your removing (even ones that don't do anything). So when removing / changing props, you need to edit the components used in the apps to make sure the builds don't fail with type errors. example of build fail due to Accordion changes. you can run `npm run build` in the root of the directory locally to see if everything still builds correctly

When I refer to kitchen sink, I am referring to something like how the charts stories are done

https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/studio/components/ui/Charts/BarChart.stories.tsx

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22714384/194909840-178cca0b-264d-4b49-b9cc-5948fc439dc7.png

@Ziinc you ever clicked on ‘Docs’ in storybook, its just a big long page of all the stories compiled together.

Is there not a best practice from Storybook to follow here?

Looks like most storybooks utilize a lot of individual stories. Github, TheGuardian, ChakraUI. https://storybook.js.org/showcase Also looks like a "kitchen sink" on each component which you get for free. example of 'collection of stories/states': https://main--61a90feace7802003a4d9c45.chromatic.com/?path=/docs/components-actionlist-features--block-description Example of individual stories https://main--61a90feace7802003a4d9c45.chromatic.com/?path=/story/components-actionlist-features--block-description

Docs mode on a per state basis would still result in friction from verbosity. 

In any case I'm ambivalent on the matter as this is bikeshedding.

> since the storybook is going to be used for reference, it would reduce friction when browsing for components and their different possible states.

Doesn't this give you exactly that?
https://main--61a90feace7802003a4d9c45.chromatic.com/?path=/docs/components-actionlist-features--block-description

and then each one of these is an isolated story as well, which can be individually controlled in the canvas tab if needed.

> Docs mode on a per state basis would still result in friction from verbosity.

Docs view is on a 'per component' basis. not a per story/state basis

ambivalence is probably not the right word. I'm neutral on any approach.

> Docs mode on a per state basis would still result in friction from verbosity.

What I mean by verbosity is [this](https://main--61a90feace7802003a4d9c45.chromatic.com/?path=/docs/components-button-features--danger). Yes all states are on one page, but to view all different states requires scrolling >5vh on my mac just for buttons. 
What The above could be solved by placing all in one story instead of splitting out into 6, cutting boilerplate and maybe even reducing one extra doc page to look at. Which is the kitchen sink style I am referring to for writing stories.
